column4: Visit note | 2025-10-06 09:00 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Wasim Mondal, 61, male. Mr. Mondal presents today complaining of bothersome dizziness whenever he looks up and a brief, sharp spinning sensation whenever he rolls over or turns in his bed. He explains that these unsettling episodes began shortly after he suffered from a viral cold in Mirpur. He works as a tailor, which requires him to sit for long hours and frequently tilt his head, making his work quite difficult lately. He has no known chronic illnesses or significant comorbidity. He denies any headaches, visual disturbances, numbness, weakness, slurred speech, or fainting spells. On examination: Dix-Hallpike test positive on the right side, along with other vitals including BP 118/79 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, and weight 70 kg. Cranial nerves are intact, and cerebellar tests show no signs of central ataxia. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued to help manage his symptoms during acute episodes. He was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown during today's session. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
